summary: Bengkulu is a province of Indonesia and a trans visitor to Bengkulu stands under Indonesia's national legal and policy framework. No region-specific signal was identified in the sources reviewed: they record no Bengkulu-specific statute, ordinance, protection measure, enforcement action or documented incident bearing on trans people, so the national assessment applies without local modification.
tangentialFactors:
The two sources assembled for Bengkulu are a general encyclopaedia entry on the province and a national-level overview of LGBTQ rights in Indonesia; neither contains material specific to Bengkulu, and the national material is carried by the parent record rather than repeated here.

One source documents a 2025 public-opinion survey reporting that 93% of Indonesians rated homosexuality morally unacceptable, alongside national enforcement events in June and August 2025; these are national figures and are not disaggregated to Bengkulu, so they indicate the surrounding climate of opinion rather than any measured provincial attitude.

outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Bengkulu has enacted its own provincial or district-level morality regulations, and whether any such instrument has been enforced against trans people, is unresolved: the sources reviewed do not address sub-national regulation in Bengkulu at all, and the absence of a documented provincial ordinance should not be read as confirmation that none exists.

No incident data, police practice, healthcare access information, or facilities situation for Bengkulu was sourced; the province's record in this dossier rests on the absence of documented material rather than on documented absence of risk.
